decision: A single `grant` authority table — the only object encoding who may do what to which resources — whose permission floor is `resource_type × operation × scope`, where `scope` is an element of a closed lattice (S, ⊑, ⊓, ⊥) over four element kinds: hierarchy-node (subtree containment), tag-set (set inclusion), numeric-interval (canonical containment), and scope-set (union of the prior), stored in canonical form. The lattice's structural, decidable, total partial order ⊑ powers a write-time subset gate (validateNarrowing): a delegated grant is rejected before persistence unless child.scope ⊑ granter.scope and its facet/constraint do not widen the parent — making monotonic narrowing provable and self-elevation structurally impossible, not merely audited. The meet ⊓ is closed (never an arbitrary predicate), which is exactly what makes ⊑ decidable; that is why the lattice is closed rather than a free-text `expr`. The genesis tenant-owner is the un-parented delegation root; free-form predicate scopes sit OUTSIDE the lattice, are owner-only, and are delegable=false. Tools, masked fields, and record-level rights are DERIVED projections of grant rows resolved by T-0021 — no second permission subsystem. Grants bind to immutable UUIDs from T-0014 ResourceRef (never slugs). Grant create/revoke emit first-class events into the T-0016 audit floor (obligation + fields only). `grant` is a T-0013 tenant table (tenant_id leading PK, FORCE RLS, default-DENY, withTenant). DESIGN-only: DDL/RLS = T-0053, resolver/PDP = T-0021, ledger = T-0016. The static-now deliverable is the pure-TS scope-lattice algebra built immediately after this ADR as a self-contained module `src/core/grant-lattice.ts` with vitest fitness tests (FF-1..FF-9); it has no DB/IO/LLM dependency and verifies the load-bearing narrowing invariant before any Postgres exists.

rejected_alternatives.option: Free-form predicate / arbitrary `expr` as the scope
rejected_alternatives.why_not: ⊑ becomes undecidable — cannot structurally prove one boolean expr implies another without a theorem prover or live-data eval; monotonic narrowing degrades to post-hoc audit and self-elevation becomes possible-but-logged. The 'was: arbitrary expr, unsound' the hypothesis §2/§6-A#2 rejected. Survives only as owner-only, non-delegable escape hatch outside the lattice (FR-6).

rejected_alternatives.option: Second authority subsystem (parallel record-ACL + separate field-visibility store)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Two sources of truth for who may touch a record/field; they drift, a permission in one but not the other is a silent leak or denial. Hypothesis §3 Q5 / §6-A#2: record-rights = operation × scope in ONE tuple, tools/fields derived. NF-1 forbids it; FF-A4 lints for it.

rejected_alternatives.option: Grant binds to slugs / display names
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Renaming a resource would silently re-target or orphan grants (T-0014 NF-3 rename-safety). Grants bind to immutable UUIDs from ResourceRef (T-0014 §5); FF-A5 lints that no node_id is a slug.

rejected_alternatives.option: Grant attaches directly to a person/agent
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Couples authority to identity; substitution, audit, least-privilege break. Grants attach to a `role` (the principal); humans and agents reach grants only through role assignments (T-0022).

rejected_alternatives.option: Post-hoc audit of self-elevation (detect-and-revoke) instead of a write-time gate
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Narrowing becomes a hope checked after damage. The closed lattice makes the subset check a pre-persistence structural decision (FR-5); a widening grant never lands. Detect-and-revoke is the discipline-not-structure anti-pattern (T-0013 §2).

rejected_alternatives.option: A ⊤ (top / 'all') element in the delegable lattice
rejected_alternatives.why_not: An implicit unbounded top makes every scope ⊑ ⊤, so any chain could widen back to 'all' through a top-typed parent. 'All' authority, if it exists, is an owner-only construct (FR-6), not a delegable lattice element; closure is stated over the delegable sublattice that EXCLUDES any implicit top. ⊥ (bottom, the well-defined empty meet) is kept; ⊤ is not.

Requires a semantic bridge between unrelated domains; there is none, and inventing one re-introduces undecidability. Distinct kinds are incomparable unless a scope-set explicitly contains a same-kind member (FR-3); meet of distinct non-set kinds is ⊥.

rejected_alternatives.option: Store scopes in raw input form; normalize only at compare time
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Comparison would depend on input member order / interval direction / duplicate tags, making ⊑/⊓ non-deterministic and fitness tests flaky. Canonical-form-at-write (NF-5) makes every stored scope normalized so comparison is order-independent and idempotent (AC-8).

rejected_alternatives.option: Mint the lattice algebra inside src/core/types.ts / jobStore.ts (edit existing files)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Collides with frozen job-model types and the in-memory store; couples authority to the job apparatus. The algebra is a NEW self-contained file src/core/grant-lattice.ts (additive, no edits to existing exports — FE-W23-0008 compatibility: types.ts/jobStore.ts public symbols untouched).

contracts: normalize(s: ScopeElement): ScopeElement — canonical form (NF-5): interval lo<=hi, tags sorted+de-duped, scope-set flattened (no nested set) with ⊑-redundant members dropped; IDEMPOTENT (normalize(normalize(s)) deep-equals normalize(s)).

isNarrowerOrEqual(child, parent, oracle): boolean — the partial order ⊑; structural, decidable, TOTAL (never throws/unknown). node⊑node via subtree containment (oracle); tags⊑tags via ⊆; interval⊑interval via same-axis containment; element⊑set iff fits one member; set⊑X iff every member ⊑ X; cross-kind non-set => false. ⊥⊑anything true.

meet(x, y, oracle): ScopeElement — greatest lower bound ⊓, CLOSED (result always node/tags/interval/set/⊥, never an arbitrary predicate). node⊓node=descendant or ⊥; tags=intersection; interval=[max lo,min hi] or ⊥; set⊓X=pairwise meets minus ⊥; distinct non-set kinds=⊥.

validateNarrowing(parent: Grant, child: Grant, oracle): {ok:true} | {ok:false; reason:'scope_widens'|'facet_widens'|'constraint_widens'|'parent_non_delegable'|'free_form_non_delegable'} — the FR-5 write-time gate, pre-persistence, no mutation. Accept iff parent.delegable AND parent.scope not freeform AND isNarrowerOrEqual(child.scope,parent.scope) AND facet/constraint non-widening. A freeform parent => free_form_non_delegable without inspecting child. Genesis tenant-owner mints are NOT subset-checked (un-parented root); every grant the owner delegates downward then becomes a subset-checked parent.

isEffective(grant: Grant, nowMs): boolean — validity-window helper (AC-13): (validFrom==null||now>=validFrom)&&(validUntil==null||now<validUntil). Out-of-window => zero capability; resolver (T-0021) treats as absent (FR-8). Single place validity is decided.

Free-form invariant (FR-6): only the genesis tenant-owner may mint a {kind:'freeform'} grant; it is forced delegable=false; any delegation whose parent is freeform is rejected; isNarrowerOrEqual against a freeform element is false for any lattice child (containment of an arbitrary predicate is unprovable).

Audit obligation (FR-7): every grant create AND revoke code path emits a GrantAuditEvent (actor, subjectRoleId, capability=resourceType×operation×resourceFacet, scope, proposedBy?/confirmedBy?) into the T-0016 audit floor; T-0018 fixes the obligation + minimum fields, not the ledger.

Build boundary: NEW self-contained file src/core/grant-lattice.ts (+ tests src/__tests__/grant-lattice.test.ts), ADDITIVE — no edit to existing exports of src/core/types.ts or src/core/jobStore.ts; no DB/IO/network/LLM import (pure functions + injected AncestryOracle). All new types declared in and exported from grant-lattice.ts.

Tenant inheritance (T-0013, NF-4): grant is a tenant table — tenant_id leading PK, FORCE RLS + default-DENY, scoped uniqueness, all access via withTenant; the subset check runs only within one tenant's grants (a tenant-B grant can never parent a tenant-A delegation).
